title: With Midterms Coming Up, G.O.P. Is Bogged Down in Congress
partialText: Republican majorities are at odds on big issues as the Senate resorts to extraordinary measures to pass homeland security funding over a Democratic blockade.

title: In Virginia Redistricting Win, Democrats Play Hardball to Thwart Trump
partialText: “We cannot bring a stick to a knife fight”: Democrats are increasingly open to extreme measures, including gerrymandering, when the stakes are high.

title: Hoarding Is Driving Energy Prices Higher Everywhere
partialText: As wealthy nations scramble to secure stocks of oil, the result is higher prices for all and shortages in vulnerable countries.

title: To Iran, Trump Blinked First by Extending the Cease-Fire
partialText: Iran’s leaders believe that they can withstand an enduring standoff longer than President Trump. The strategy could be economically devastating for average Iranians.

title: A $440,000 Breast Reduction: How Doctors Cashed In on the No Surprises Act and Arbitration
partialText: A law meant to end surprise medical billing accidentally created a multibillion-dollar industry that is making doctors richer.

title: Pace of N.I.H. Funding Slows Further in Trump’s Second Year
partialText: The agency has approved far fewer new grants than it did in years past. A renewed effort to screen for disfavored terms and a loss of personnel are contributing.

title: Kevin Warsh, Trump’s Fed Pick, Has Tough Task Shedding ‘Sock Puppet’ Label
partialText: Kevin M. Warsh, at his confirmation hearing to lead the Federal Reserve, sought to dispel doubts that he would yield to President Trump’s demand for lower rates.

title: A Capitol Police Officer, Bogus Accusations and a Jan. 6 Conspiracy Theory
partialText: Shauni Kerkhoff was wrongfully implicated in the notorious Capitol Hill pipe-bomb case. Can she ever fully move on?

title: Anthropic’s New Mythos A.I. Model Sets Off Global Alarms
partialText: Mythos has triggered emergency responses from central banks and intelligence agencies globally, as Anthropic decides who has access to the powerful model.

title: Leaked Code for Anthropic’s Claude Code Tests Copyright Challenges in A.I. Era
partialText: Artificial intelligence tools are making it faster than ever to reproduce creative work. Does copyright even matter anymore?

title: Musk’s SpaceX Goals Shift Ahead of Its I.P.O.
partialText: As SpaceX prepares to go public, Mr. Musk has proposed moonshots that differ from the company’s original aim of reaching Mars.

title: College Where Charlie Kirk Was Killed Revokes Graduation Speaker’s Invite
partialText: Utah Valley University was thrilled that Sharon McMahon, a best-selling author, would speak at its graduation. And then her old posts resurfaced.

title: Supreme Court Rejects Oil Company Argument in Fight Over Great Lakes Pipeline
partialText: The justices sided with Michigan officials, who have raised environmental alarms and pushed to decommission an aging section of the pipeline.

title: Supreme Court Finds Soldier Injured in Suicide Bombing Can Sue
partialText: An American soldier was injured in a 2016 suicide bombing in Afghanistan. The justices cleared the way for the soldier to proceed with a lawsuit against a military contractor.

title: Aftershocks from ‘The Shadow Papers’
partialText: Publication of a trove of confidential Supreme Court memos ignited debates in the legal academy.

title: ‘Free Births’ Are a New Pregnancy Trend. Critics Warn About Serious Risks.
partialText: Promoters of free birthing reject any type of medical intervention during pregnancy or delivery. The movement has been trending on social media, but critics warn it poses serious risks.

title: Dark Skies and Dark Energy Converge in West Texas
partialText: In the Big Bend region, a portal to the early universe is enabled by the largest dark-sky reserve on Earth.

title: There’s Another Reason Gen Z Can’t Find Work
partialText: It’s not just because of A.I. This started 40 years ago.

title: ‘The Rich Don’t Play by the Rules. So Why Should I?’
partialText: Why petty theft might be the new political protest.

title: Pope Leo Is Skipping Some of Africa’s Biggest Catholic Nations
partialText: As the pontiff arrives in the tiny authoritarian nation of Equatorial Guinea, some Catholics in Africa say they are excited about his visit but are feeling a little left out.

title: California Is Rife With Hospice Fraud. But Whose Fault Is It?
partialText: The Trump administration and Democratic state leaders are blaming each other for what everyone agrees is a big problem. The president has targeted California and Gov. Gavin Newsom in particular.

title: F.A.A. Investigates Near Miss Between Passenger Jets at J.F.K. Airport
partialText: An American Airlines regional jet flew close to an Air Canada regional jet after aborting its landing. It was the second such incident in recent days at a major U.S. airport.

title: Japan Is Used to Earthquakes, but What About a Big One?
partialText: For many people in Japan, the country’s regular tremors are not a big deal. Officials are urging them to prepare for the next catastrophic quake.
